title: fix(mcp): an MCP tool call repeating a unique value answers UNIQUE_VIOLATION, not the engine's DUPLICATE_RECORD (#23701)
body:
Fixes #23701
Clause-②: no

An MCP tool call that repeats a unique value now answers the ruled wire spelling, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, in its `isError` tool result, instead of the engine's in-process `DUPLICATE_RECORD`. Only the code moves.

## Governing text

Maintainer ruling, recorded in commit `65846bc46`, as restated at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`:

> Maintainer ruling (2026-09-03, recorded in commit 65846bc46): one wire spelling on every route, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`; the row reports it too.

The engine's thrown identity is not renamed: `DuplicateRecordError.code` stays `DUPLICATE_RECORD` in-process. A producer that merely speaks `DUPLICATE_RECORD` (a hook or an action handler throwing the registered code without being the engine's class) keeps its own code.

## What changed

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, in `thrownRefusalEnvelope`, decided before the code is written:

- **Key.** `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope(err)`, the existing `@objectstack/types` predicate (already a dependency of this package) that `RestServer`'s arm, the batch and import rows, both Hono doors (PR #23682) and the dispatcher (PR #23700) ask: the registered code AND the class name, never message text. No second translator.
- **Code.** For that class, the module-local `wireCodeOf` reads the code off the shared classification's arm, `structuredCodeAnswer` (an existing `@objectstack/types` export, the arm `RestServer` answers with), which states `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` for it. Every other throw keeps its thrown code. This package spells no copy of the wire code of its own; see "Spelling" below for why.
- **One writer.** `thrownRefusalEnvelope` is what `errorResultWithCode` (the data tools and `list_actions`), `errorResultFromThrown` (`run_action`, `resume_run`) and the record resource (`MCPServerRuntime.bridgeResources`) all read. Both transports (Streamable HTTP and stdio) register the same tools through `wireBridgeTools`, so both get the branch.
- **Unchanged.** The result stays an `isError` tool result, `status` stays `409`, `message` is the engine's sentence as before, and the envelope's keys stay `code`, `message`, `status`. `thrownRefusalEnvelope`'s signature and the exported `ThrownRefusalEnvelope` interface are unchanged. No export is added. No `packages/types`, `packages/runtime` or `packages/spec` file moves.

### The context slot: measured, there is none, so the code alone is carried

The other doors also carry the REST arm's context (`developerMessage`, `object`, and `field` when the driver named the column) in their envelope's `details`. This envelope has no such slot:

- `ThrownRefusalEnvelope` is `code`, `message`, `status` (optional). It reads no `details`.
- The data tools (`create_record`, `update_record`, and the rest) withhold `details` by design. `errorResultWithCode`'s docblock says what a refusal's `details` may disclose is decided per class at the HTTP boundary, that this package holds no copy of that policy, and that `code`, `message` and `status` are what every boundary serves.
- `errorResultFromThrown` (`run_action`, `resume_run`) relays the thrown value's OWN `details`. `DuplicateRecordError` has none, so no measured body carries any.
- The record resource answers `error`, `code` and `status`.

Measured on the rig below: every positive body's keys are exactly `code`, `message`, `status`, before and after. At the other doors `details.developerMessage` is the engine's `message` byte for byte, which this envelope already carries as `message`. Whether `object` and `field` should be added on this surface is the open question at the end.

### Spelling

The first spelling at `33683617f` was a module constant, `'UNIQUE_VIOLATION' satisfies ErrorCode`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:error-code-provenance` read it as a new emitter: `FAIL — 1 stamp site(s) of a registered code with no provenance row: @objectstack/mcp stamps 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION' (constdef) at packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:389`. Its remedy is a ledger row or a `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` entry, both `packages/spec` edits outside this card's declared surface. So `da084ab11` reads the code off `structuredCodeAnswer` instead: the stamp stays where the provenance ledger already lists it (`@objectstack/types`), and this door relays the classification's answer, as the REST door does. The gate is green on it (`OK — every registered-code stamp site is listed under its own owner key or carries a recorded waiver`). Behaviour is the same on every measured row.

## Measured before and after (H1, H3)

Rig (scratch, not committed): the real `MCPServerRuntime` (from `packages/mcp` source) behind the real `HttpDispatcher`'s `/mcp` route (`dispatch()` with a Fetch `Request`, the identity step stubbed to a member), over a real `ObjectQL` with `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) and a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`. The metadata service is a listing double. The object `udoc` declares `email` unique, and `r1` holds the value. Before is the merge base `69351e985` (unfixed). After is the final head `da084ab11`.

| Tool call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `create_record` on `udoc` repeating `email` | `200`, `isError`, `{"error":{"code":"DUPLICATE_RECORD","message":"Duplicate record refused on 'udoc': a unique constraint already holds these values. No record was written.","status":409}}` | the same body with `"code":"UNIQUE_VIOLATION"` |
| `update_record` giving `r2` the value `r1` holds | the same `DUPLICATE_RECORD` body | the same, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` |
| `run_action`: a registered handler whose `ctx.engine.insert` repeats `email` | the same `DUPLICATE_RECORD` body | the same, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` |
| `run_action`: a declarative `operation: 'update'` action on `r2` | the same `DUPLICATE_RECORD` body | the same, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` |

A `diff` of the before and after outputs shows exactly these four `code` lines. Every other byte is identical, the controls included. The store is unchanged in both runs: one row holds the value, and `r2` keeps its own.

No measured body carries `field`. The unique index on this tenancy-scoped object is the composite `uniq_udoc_organization_id_email`, so the driver names no single column. This envelope would not carry it anyway (above).

## Tool census (H2, H3)

| Tool (writer) | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `create_record` (`errorResultWithCode`) | crosses: measured, pinned |
| `update_record` (`errorResultWithCode`) | crosses: measured, pinned |
| `run_action` (`errorResultFromThrown`), a handler write or a declarative update | crosses: measured, pinned |
| `resume_run` (`errorResultFromThrown`) | writer pinned directly. NOT MEASURED on a real engine: `packages/mcp` composes no engine and `packages/runtime` composes no automation service. By reading, a resumed run's write does not reach this writer as the engine's class: the flow engine rethrows a node failure as a plain `Error` (`Node 'x' failed: …`), and `classifyResumeResult` answers the failed run as `400 FLOW_FAILED`. |
| `run_action` on a `type: 'flow'` action | not crossing, by reading: the same flow-failure path, `FLOW_FAILED` |
| `delete_record`, `get_record`, `query_records`, `aggregate_records`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`, `list_objects`, `list_actions` (`errorResultWithCode`) | translate by construction (same writer). None of these calls writes a unique value. Not measured |
| the record resource | translates by construction. It is a read, so no measured call reaches it. Pinned, as the reader's second consumer |
| the stdio face | the same tools through `wireBridgeTools`. `stdio-data-bridge`'s `create` and `update` call `engine.insert` and `engine.update`, whose throw reaches the same writer. By reading, not measured separately |
| a batch tool | there is none |

## Controls

| Control (rig) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `run_action`: a handler throws `{ code: 'DUPLICATE_RECORD', status: 409 }`, not the engine's class | `DUPLICATE_RECORD`, 409 | the same |
| `create_record` on an object whose `beforeInsert` hook throws `{ code: 'DUPLICATE_RECORD', status: 409 }` | `DUPLICATE_RECORD`, 409 | the same |
| `run_action`: a handler's `ctx.engine.delete` hits a `restrict` lookup | `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, 409 | the same |
| `delete_record` on the restricted parent | `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, 409 | the same |

## Pins

New file `packages/mcp/src/mcp-unique-violation-wire-code.test.ts`, 11 rows. The tools run on the HTTP `/mcp` face (`handleHttpRequest` over the real Streamable HTTP transport), and the record resource through a real `Client` over `InMemoryTransport`. A bridge double throws a value shaped like the engine's class (`name`, `code`, `status`, `httpStatus`, `object`, `field`, its in-process `developerMessage`, a driver error on `cause`), because this package composes no engine. Codes and key presence are asserted, never wording.

- `create_record`, `update_record`, `run_action`, `resume_run`: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, `status` 409, `isError`, keys exactly `code`, `message`, `status`. Neither `DUPLICATE_RECORD` nor the driver's text appears in the result text.
- The record resource: `code` `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, `status` 409, keys exactly `code`, `error`, `status`.
- CONTROL: a producer that merely speaks `DUPLICATE_RECORD` keeps it, on `create_record`, `run_action` and the resource.
- CONTROL: the class name with another code (`CONCURRENT_UPDATE`) keeps that code.
- CONTROL: `DELETE_RESTRICTED` on `delete_record` and `run_action` keeps its code and keys.

## Ablation

At `da084ab11`, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, under an outer `trap … EXIT INT TERM` that restores the absolute path with `git checkout HEAD --`. The key line `if (!isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope(err)) return thrownCode;` was replaced by `return thrownCode; // ABLATION_23701_NO_WIRE_MAP`.

- On disk: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `378ec1bff879` to `05d1d36e1f14`.
- The pins and the rig import the MCP source by relative path (`@objectstack/mcp` is not resolved through `dist/` in either), so no rebuild was needed. `@objectstack/types` is unmutated.
- Pins: `Tests 5 failed | 6 passed (11)`. Exactly the 5 positive rows were red, each `expected 'DUPLICATE_RECORD' to be 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION'`. All 6 controls were green.
- Rig: the 8 shared rows are byte-identical to the before run at the merge base.
- Restore: the blob equals HEAD (`378ec1bff879`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty on the path.

The same ablation at `33683617f` (the first spelling) read the same: 5 red, 6 green, the rig back to the before bytes.

## Tests

At the final head `da084ab11`. `origin/main` is still the merge base `69351e985`, so there was nothing to merge.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test`: `Test Files 40 passed (40)`, `Tests 478 passed (478)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp typecheck`: exit 0. That is `tsc --noEmit` and then `check:test-typecheck: OK`, with no new debt. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file.
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/mcp`: exit 0, no findings. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp build`: exit 0 (`check-dts-emitted`: 2/2).

## Gates

Local, at the final head `da084ab11`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths: **63** commands derived from the 3 changed paths (merge base `69351e985`). All 63 ran, each exit code recorded before any pipe, and all 63 exited 0.
- `--ran` reconciliation: `63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero: all 63 recorded an exit code and none is 3).
- Among them, all exit 0: `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `pnpm check:engine-double-contract`, `pnpm check:test-source-alias`, `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `pnpm check:issue-citations`, `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `pnpm check:published-files`, `pnpm check:type-check-debt`, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-empty-changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major`.
- On the first pass at `33683617f`, two of the 63 did not measure, and both were re-run: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, no workspace `dist/`), then 0 after a cache-backed `pnpm turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2` (`75 successful`, `74 cached`); `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` exited 1 on an `ENOENT` for a scratch rig file deleted mid-sweep (not a gate verdict), then 0. At the final head both exited 0 on the first pass.
- The four artifact-roster gates whose roster sits in a directory this diff touches, plus the provenance gate, all exit 0 at the final head: `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `pnpm check:authz-resolver`, `pnpm check:error-code-casing`, `pnpm check:filter-alias-parity`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:error-code-provenance` (see "Spelling" for its first-spelling red).
- Consumer suites: the gates name none. No consumer test pins `DUPLICATE_RECORD` on an MCP tool result (`git grep` over the tests of this package's four dependents: `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, `packages/qa/dogfood` and `examples/app-todo`). `@objectstack/verify`'s `DUPLICATE_RECORD` pins are the engine's in-process system door, which does not move. Not run locally; dogfood is the full battery's.
- Every family CI runs on this PR is reported on its check-runs.

## Found, not fixed here

- **A `run_action` over a sandboxed action body still answers `DUPLICATE_RECORD`.** Measured on the rig at `da084ab11`: a `type: 'script'` action whose `body` (bound by `bindAppArtifactHandlers`, with `capabilities: ['api.write']`) calls `ctx.api.object('udoc').insert(…)` repeating `email` answered `{"error":{"code":"DUPLICATE_RECORD","message":"action 'sbx_duplicate' threw: DuplicateRecordError: Duplicate record refused on 'udoc': …","status":409}}`. The refusal leaves the sandbox without the class name, so the shared key does not match. That is the sandbox relay's question, which #23702 carries (triage ruled direction A there). #23702 is not addressed here.

## Acceptance notes

- **The provenance ledger does not see the two landed door translations.** `check:error-code-provenance` declares itself blind to a ternary, and the dispatcher (`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`) and the Hono doors (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`) stamp `'UNIQUE_VIOLATION'` inside one. `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` lists `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` under `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/driver-memory` and `@objectstack/driver-sql` only. Observation, outside this file surface, no carrier.
- The record resource now answers `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` for the engine's class too, because it reads the same envelope. It is a read, so no measured call reaches it. It is pinned so the change is declared rather than silent.
- `wireCodeOf` keeps the thrown code when the arm answers no string code. That branch is unreachable today, because the arm is gated on the same two-part predicate. If the arm ever stopped answering for this class, this door would relay `DUPLICATE_RECORD` again, and the pins here would go red.
- Docs: no edit. `content/docs/releases/` is untouched.

## Open question for the seat

The context slot. **A** (this PR): the code alone, and the envelope keeps `code`, `message`, `status` on every tool. **B**: add the arm's `object` and `field` in `details` on `run_action` and `resume_run` only, where a `details` member exists. That gives two bodies for one refusal across tools. **C**: add them on every tool. That reverses the data tools' declared withholding for this class, and it is a second wire change. Recommended: **A**, because the dispatch said to carry the code alone where there is no slot, `message` already carries what `developerMessage` would, and B or C would widen a surface nobody has measured a reader for.
